title: Attorney General of Nevada

context.text: The seat is open: Democratic incumbent Aaron Ford is term-limited and running for governor.
Cannizzaro, the state Senate majority leader, won the June 9 Democratic primary with 61.7% over Zach Conine (34.4%). Guzmán Fralick won the Republican primary with 59.9% over Danny Tarkanian (34.8%).

The Nevada Independent describes the race as a longtime prosecutor and state senator against a lawyer who has never held elected office. Suing the federal government is a central theme; the paper reports Ford has been a plaintiff in almost 90 lawsuits across both Trump terms.

Clark County's official Nov. 3, 2026 contest and candidate list (Aug. 24, 2026) shows two candidates for Attorney General: Nicole Jeanette Cannizzaro (Democratic) and Adriana Guzmán Fralick (Republican).

candidates.name: Nicole Cannizzaro
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary over Zach Conine.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists issue areas: public safety, protecting reproductive rights, taking on big corporations and protecting customers, fighting federal overreach, clean energy and environment, and civil and voting rights.

Says she would submit a budget request to bolster the attorney general's Medicaid fraud unit, would continue lawsuits against big technology companies, and would support a dispute-resolution process for public-records requests.

record.text: Voted for Attorney General Ford's 2025 bill to criminalize price fixing of essential goods, which Gov. Lombardo vetoed, and says she stands by that vote.
Supported the 2019 bill that raised the dollar amount making theft a felony from $650 to $1,200.

Gov. Lombardo's 2025 crime bill was proposed while she was Senate majority leader; she points to its crackdown on "smash-and-grab" burglaries, and a provision lowering the felony theft threshold to $750 did not make the final version.

candidates.name: Adriana Guzmán Fralick
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary over Danny Tarkanian; endorsed by President Trump.
candidates.currentRole: Attorney; runs a law firm in Reno

priorities.text: Campaign site lists: tougher sentencing, cracking down on drugs, backing the blue, helping domestic violence victims, improving school safety, ending child exploitation, stopping sanctuary cities, government transparency and securing elections.
Would roll back provisions of 2019's AB 236 and lower the felony theft threshold, which she called "a big mistake" to have raised.

Would seek passage of a "SAVE Nevada Act" that her site says would count all ballots on election day, remove non-citizens from voter rolls, eliminate automatic voter registration and end universal mail-in ballots.

statements.quote: Local authorities must be free to work with federal immigration officials to keep dangerous criminals off our streets.
statements.context: On her campaign site, in opposing sanctuary policies; she does not address expanding deportations

statements.quote: Adriana will ensure that no illegal immigrants are registered to vote and will prosecute any cases of voter fraud.
statements.context: On her campaign site; she does not say whether she would require documentary proof of citizenship

statements.quote: Adriana will stand shoulder to shoulder with police and sheriffs across the state to ensure they have the resources, training, and legal backing they need.

researchNotes: Slate: confirmed against Clark County's official general-election contest list (the Secretary of State's site blocks automated access); it matches Ballotpedia. Cannizzaro's campaign site lists issue-area headings only (no text), so her stances come from The Nevada Independent's questionnaire, where several answers were not a clear yes or no and are not recorded as stances. Cannizzaro's record items come from that outlet's account of her votes, not roll-call pages. Official Legislature roll calls for her votes were not reachable.
